court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Basti - O.S. No. 15 of 2010
case_name: Gulabpati vs Smt. Pushpa Rani Pandey And 2 Ors.

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Pushpa Rani Pandey and 2 others

facts_of_case: Plaintiff-appellant Gulabpati filed a suit for declaration that she is the legally wedded wife of Murli Prasad @ Murlidhar and entitled to receive family pension. She alleged that her husband joined Air Force, reduced her status to a domestic servant, and neglected her and their minor daughter.

legal_principles.principle: A document cannot be marked as an exhibit unless it is admitted in evidence.
legal_principles.held: According to counsel for appellant until and unless a document is admitted in evidence, it cannot be marked as exhibit
cited_cases: New Okhla Industrial Development Authority Vs. Kendriya Karamchari Sahkari Grih Nirman Samiti Ltd., (2017) 4 UPLBEC 3077

legal_principles.principle: A court cannot proceed to decide a matter based on documents that have not been admitted in evidence.
legal_principles.held: Infact there is not a single evidence admitted by Court in accordance with procedure prescribed in Order 13 CPC read with General Rules (Civil), 1957'
cited_cases: New Okhla Industrial Development Authority Vs. Kendriya Karamchari Sahkari Grih Nirman Samiti Ltd., (2017) 4 UPLBEC 3077

outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed, and the judgment of the trial court was set aside.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for maintenance under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
preparing an appeal against a family court judgment
understanding the role of Section 19 in Family Court Act, 1984
